title: Active-learning experiments reveal distinct on-field and off-field polarization-switching behavior in ferroelectrics
summary: An active-learning workflow paired with automated piezoresponse-force microscopy discovered relationships between local ferroelectric domain structure and polarization-switching hysteresis. The experimentally selected sampling paths and points differed substantially between on-field and off-field hysteresis loops, indicating that the two measurement modes are dominated by different mechanisms. The result applies to the reported ferroelectric sample and spectroscopy workflow; it does not establish a universal mechanism for all ferroelectrics.
ai_technology: Machine-learning active-learning framework for automated piezoresponse force microscopy and spectroscopy
organization: Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago; Nagoya Institute of Technology and collaborators

evidence.tested: An active-learning workflow paired with automated piezoresponse-force microscopy discovered relationships between local ferroelectric domain structure and polarization-switching hysteresis.
evidence.unknown: The authors report experimental correlation and different on-field/off-field discovery paths, interpreting this as evidence that the measurement modes are dominated by different mechanisms. The study does not establish a universal causal account across materials; it reports a specific automated PFM/spectroscopy investigation.
evidence.ai_role: The model learned correlations between high-dimensional local domain structure and hysteresis-loop switching characteristics, and used loop descriptors and uncertainty to guide the automated microscopy and spectroscopy measurements. Human physics insight was encoded in the acquisition function.
